subject: Post-call: deployment pathway & dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>

Subject: Post-call: deployment pathway & sizing

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we committed to follow up on. TL;DR: Novella's primary need is consistent <20ms p50 for short text lookups (search/semantic) and ~200ms p95 for longer generation flows. Your stated day-to-day will be a mix of short embeddings/lookups plus bursty generative flows tied to promotions.

Key notes from call:
- Current expected peak TPS (in steady state): 120 TPS for short requests (avg 40 tokens)
- Peak concurrent long-generation flows: ~18 simultaneous requests (avg 450 tokens) during campaigns
- Token mix estimate: ~78% short (<64 tokens), ~15% medium (64–256), ~7% long (>256) — Aaron to confirm exact numbers by EOD 4/22
- Data residency: US-based production; potential private VPC requirement for some regulated enterprise customers later this year

Options we discussed and our preliminary guidance:
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, but with less capacity isolation during your campaign bursts — could be fine for initial rollout if cost/timeliness is critical
- Dedicated capacity: best fit if you need predictable throughput and isolation for campaign spikes; we can size a reserved GPU pool to meet your p50/p95 targets without constant scaling churn
- Private (VPC/on-prem): recommended only if you must keep model and inference inside your network for compliance — we'll need a separate architecture discussion if you go this route

Immediate asks / next steps (who does what):
1) Aaron — please send exact weekly traffic patterns and any historical peak-day multipliers by 2027-04-22 EOD (we used your rough numbers above)
2) Marissa / Karthik — we'll propose a 2-size dedicated pool (min / target) and map to GPU families with estimated monthly reserved cost and expected p50/p95: deliver by 4/23
3) Diego — schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk Novella through the worksheet and run a short what-if sensitivity table (I've proposed two times below)

Attachments: shared a blank capacity worksheet template (we'll populate it once Aaron shares token distribution).

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few numbers now so you can proceed:

- Steady-state short TPS: 110–130 TPS (we see 120 most days)
- Burst pattern: during campaign peaks we see the short TPS double for about 45–90 minutes; long-generation concurrent requests can jump to 25 for 10–20 minutes
- Token mix: Aaron attached a CSV with a sample distribution (see attachment in his reply); roughly matches your breakdown but swaps medium/long a bit in bursts
- Compliance: for now US-only; we may need a VPC path for a couple of enterprise pilots in Q4 but not a blocker for initial rollout

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>

Subject: RE: Post-call: deployment pathway & sizing (recommended dedicated config)

Samantha / team — quick follow-up from our side after reviewing the numbers Diego captured and Aaron's sample token distribution. I kept the note focused on recommended GPU families and concurrency knobs so you can see the tradeoffs.

Principles: keep short request latency low by avoiding too-large batching on those paths; use a separate pool for long generations to avoid KV cache pollution and to tune longer-sequence kernels.

Recommended dedicated setup (initial commit):
- Short-pool (search/lookups): 4 x A100s (or 6 x H100s if you want headroom for growth) with a low-latency serving profile. Target: 120–250 TPS range with p50 <20ms, p95 <60ms.
- Long-pool (generations/campaigns): 3 x A100s (or 2 x H100s) configured with larger batch windows and expanded KV cache. Target: handle 25 concurrent long gen at ~450 tokens with p95 ~200–300ms depending on model size.

Concurrency & batching guidance:
- Short-pool: aggressive small-batch (batch size 4–8), token-by-token streaming enabled; concurrency caps per-GPU to avoid queueing (we'll calculate exact per-GPU concurrency in the worksheet)
- Long-pool: larger batch windows, allow higher per-request token budgets, and separate autoscaling policy for sustained campaign windows

Cost / ops trade: A100 baseline is more cost-efficient for sustained reserved workloads; H100 gives overhead for model families and headroom for future ops but is >30% higher reservation. We can show an apples-to-apples reserved cost sheet in the attachment.

I've populated the attached dedicated_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx with two scenarios (conservative / target). Also included a small token_mix_samples.csv with the adjusted burst distribution Aaron mentioned.

If this looks reasonable we'll finalize recommended reserved counts and a rollout plan for canary traffic.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
